Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api

Interface RulesEngine<O>

Type Parameters:
O - The output object type to instantiate
All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractRulesEngine, StatefulRulesEngine, StatelessRulesEngine
public interface RulesEngine<O>
The RulesEngine fires the action expression from a list of Rule objects when their conditions evaluate to true.

  • Method Details

    • setRuleList

      void setRuleList(List<Rule> ruleList)
      Set the rule list for use in processing rules through the rules engine
      Parameters:
      ruleList - The list of Rule objects
      Throws:
      RuleCompilationException - if a rule fails to compile, has a null or blank condition or action, has a condition that contains an assignment, or if the list contains a null rule
      NullPointerException - if ruleList itself is null

    • run

      O run(FactStore<Object> facts)
      Fire rules engine against the rules supplied by the rules list.
      Parameters:
      facts - The key/value fact store to run the rule engine against.
      Returns:
      The output of firing the actions of the matching Rule objects, or null if the rule list is empty or no rule matched
      Throws:
      RuleExecutionException - if a rule fails during evaluation
      IllegalStateException - if setRuleList(List) has not been called
      NullPointerException - if facts is null

    • addImports

      RulesEngine<O> addImports(Set<String> packages)
      This method adds package imports to the ParserContext in order to speed up the execution of rules and simplify the rule expression. You may want to use this if many of your rules require the same packages.
      Parameters:
      packages - A set of packages to import
      Returns:
      A reference to this rules engine. This enables the use of the builder design pattern

    • addImport

      RulesEngine<O> addImport(String packageString)
      This adds a single package to the ParserContext in order to speed up the execution of rules and simplify the rule expression. Add the fully qualified name of the package as a string. You may want to use this if many of your rules require the same packages.
      Parameters:
      packageString - The package to import. Example: "java.util"
      Returns:
      A reference to this rules engine. This enables the use of the builder design pattern
